blocks.text: Sometimes we wish to apply the concept of momentum to cases where the applied force is not constant, it acts for very short time. For example, when a bat hits a cricket ball, the force certainly varies from instant to instant during the collision. In such cases, it is more convenient to deal with the product of force and time (F⃗ × t) instead of either quantity alone. The product of average force F that acts during time t is called impulse given by
